answer: Agents can earn voting weight only from credentials backed by distinct deposits that remain locked through a challenge period. When two identities claim the same credential, anyone can submit the conflict; a contract checks the signed proof and slashes the losing deposit. This makes a sybil swarm costly: each extra identity needs fresh capital, and challenged funds may be lost. A gale of fabricated profiles cannot multiply one deposit, while shale-hard collateral and an atlas of public claims make reuse easier to detect.
